Subject: Postdoctoral Position Available in Occupancy Change Modeling and Forecasting

Sorry for the impersonal email and feel free to circulate.


 I'm looking for a postdoctoral researcher to work with me on an exciting piece of the Grinnell Resurvey Project.  The ideal person would start before the end of the year or early next year.  Fuller description is below and attached.


Postdoctoral Position in Occupancy Change Modeling and Forecasting

 

A postdoctoral researcher position is available with the Grinnell Resurvey Project under the direction of Professor Steve Beissinger at UC Berkeley in the Museum of Vertebrate Zoology (MVZ) and collaborators. This project is funded by NSF to model the effects of climate and land-use change on avian communities in California at sites originally visited by Joseph Grinnell and colleagues in the early 20th century.  

 

This position will require implementation of hierarchical multispecies occupancy models that account for imperfect detection as well as methods for forecasting the impacts of future climate and land-use change. Candidates should have experience analyzing large ecological data sets including occupancy modeling, implemented in Bayesian frameworks using Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation. Experience with land-use and climate change modeling, and machine-learning methods are a plus.

 

The ideal candidate will have:

-         

·        A doctoral degree in a relevant subject with a strong record of scientific publications

  • Experience in Bayesian and high performance computing (e.g. JAGS, NIMBLE, STAN, cloud computing)
  • Advanced knowledge of R and additional programming languages
  • Skills in spatial modeling and GIS
  • Demonstrated ability to learn and implement new quantitative approaches and think creatively about connections between organisms, places, and people
  • Ability to work both independently and as part of a team

This position has flexibility for working remotely or at Berkeley, and includes competitive salary and health benefits. It is a full-time, 12-month, fixed-term position, with possible reappointment for a second year conditional on satisfactory performance and funding. Position available immediately, but will consider applicants that can not start until 2021. US citizenship or current visa required.

 

Review of applications begins Oct. 12  and is rolling until the position is filled. Interested candidates should send (1) an email describing their research interests and qualifications along with (2) a CV, (3) representative publications, and (4) contact information for two references to Steve Beissinger: be...@berkeley.edu. 

 Steve
